title: Isolation verification playbook and synthetic audit harness
creator: Marco Li
description: Create a repeatable playbook and an automated synthetic audit harness that validates tenant isolation and residency guarantees for Dedicated capacity. The harness will synthesize tenant workloads across multiple geo regions, exercise retention and export paths, capture cryptographic snapshots of node topology and storage manifests, and produce a signed compliance dossier usable for audits. Scope includes: test scenarios, KMS signing integration, retention mapping verification, evidence packaging, and automation to run on schedule and on-demand.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic harness can run a configurable suite of tenant workload scenarios spanning at least 3 region profiles (US-east, EU-west, AP-south)
Automated collector produces time-stamped snapshots containing node IDs, IP ranges, volume IDs, and model variant metadata in a canonical JSON format
All snapshots are signed via customer or platform KMS and verifiable offline with provided public keys
Retention mapping verifier flags mismatches between tenant-configured retention and actual object lifecycle policies
A generated compliance dossier (PDF + tar.gz) is available with links to raw snapshots, signing metadata, and an evidence manifest; end-to-end run completes without manual steps
Playbook documentation includes run instructions, failure modes, and remediation actions for SRE and Compliance teams

Implementation: collector service to snapshot node and storage state (Aisha)
Integration: KMS signing flow and key rotation compatibility (Priya)
Verification: retention policy checker for S3/GCS/Blob backends (Diego)
Packaging: evidence manifest format and dossier generator (Grace)
Automation: CI job + on-demand runbook + schedule in airflow or jobs service (Ravi)
Docs: playbook markdown and runbook in Confluence (Marco)
E2E Tests: cross-region synthetic run and manual QA (Aisha)
Rollout: feature flag gating and canary to internal orgs (SRE)
Postmortem template for any harness failures (Aisha)
decisions: Will use platform KMS by default with opt-in for customer-managed keys after security review
Evidence manifest will use a compact canonical JSON schema v1.0 to simplify verification and archival
Snapshots will be stored in a time-partitioned tenant bucket and retained according to the tenant's retention setting plus a 30-day audit buffer
Signing metadata will include KMS key ID, signing algorithm, timestamp, and a SHA-256 digest of the snapshot payload
